title: Fully marked parameter mapping cores and anodyne restriction
statement:
Use the simplicial sets, standard simplices and universes of [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones] and [def-weil-size-convention]. A marked simplicial set is a pair $(X,M_X)$ with $M_X\subseteq X_1$ containing all degenerate edges; morphisms preserve marked edges. Products mark precisely pairs of marked edges. Write $K^ lat$ for a simplicial set with only its degenerate edges marked and $K^\sharp$ for one with every edge marked. Use quasicategories, equivalences and cores as in [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones]. For a quasicategory $C$ write $C^
atural$ for its equivalences marked and $C^\simeq$ for its simplicial subset whose simplices have every edge an equivalence. For marked $X,Y$ define $\operatorname{Map}^\sharp(X,Y)_n=\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathrm{sSet}^+}(X	imes(\Delta^n)^\sharp,Y)$. For every simplicial set $K$ there is a natural identity $$\operatorname{Map}^\sharp(K^\sharp,C^
atural)=\operatorname{Fun}(K,C^\simeq),$$ where $\operatorname{Fun}(K,T)_n=\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathrm{sSet}}(K	imes\Delta^n,T)$. It identifies a marked map with the same underlying map factored through $C^\simeq$, and respects restriction in $K$ and maps of quasicategories $C$. If $j:K\hookrightarrow L$ is a degreewise injective weak homotopy equivalence in the Kan model structure of [lem-coef-kan-quillen-right-proper], then restriction $$\operatorname{Map}^\sharp(L^\sharp,C^
atural)\longrightarrow\operatorname{Map}^\sharp(K^\sharp,C^
atural)$$ is a trivial Kan fibration, equivalently has the right lifting property against every boundary inclusion $\partial\Delta^n\hookrightarrow\Delta^n$, including $n=0$. No nonemptiness assumption on $K,L$ or $C$ is required. The identity and restriction assertion are relative to the input universe.

proof.text: For every $n\geq0$, the product marking on $K^\sharp\times(\Delta^n)^\sharp$ marks every edge: both coordinates of any product edge are marked. Thus a map from this marked product to $C^\natural$ is exactly a simplicial map $h:K\times\Delta^n\to C$ carrying every edge to an equivalence. For every simplex $\sigma$ of the product, all edges of $h\sigma$ are then equivalences, so $h\sigma$ belongs to the core $C^\simeq$ of [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones]. Conversely, a map into this core carries every edge to an equivalence. Factoring through the simplicial subset $C^\simeq\subseteq C$ is unique. This gives the required degreewise bijection, including degree zero.

source.place: Section 3.1.3, mapping formulas; direct reconstruction of the fully marked source case.

proof.text: Under these bijections, the operator associated to $\alpha:[m]\to[n]$ is on both sides precomposition by $\mathrm{id}_K\times\Delta(\alpha)$. The bijections therefore form the stated identity of simplicial sets. Restriction along $u:K^{\prime}\to K$ is on both sides precomposition by $u\times\mathrm{id}$. If $v:C\to D$ is a map of quasicategories, it sends an inverse edge and its two inverse-triangle witnesses to the corresponding witnesses in $D$, so sends equivalences to equivalences and restricts to $v^\simeq:C^\simeq\to D^\simeq$. Both sides send $h$ to the same underlying map $vh$. This proves both naturalities with the normalization in the statement.

source.place: Section 3.1.3, mapping formulas; restriction and postcomposition checked on the identical maps.

proof.text: Put $E=C^\simeq$. Since $C$ is a quasicategory, [lem-cbc-enhanced-functor-cone-calculus] states that its core $E$ is Kan. Thus the map $E\to\Delta^0$ is a Kan fibration. This uses no nonemptiness condition: the Kan condition tests horns only in positive dimensions.

source.place: Proposition 1.2.5.3, maximal Kan subcomplex; existing enhanced-calculus statement supplies this input.

proof.text:
By [lem-coef-kan-quillen-right-proper], the degreewise injective weak homotopy equivalence $j:K\hookrightarrow L$ is a trivial cofibration of the Kan model structure. Its lifting axiom against fibrations says precisely that $j$ is anodyne in the sense of [lem-coef-sset-anodyne-pushout-product], namely it has the left lifting property against every Kan fibration. For $n\geq0$, the boundary inclusion $b_n:\partial\Delta^n\hookrightarrow\Delta^n$ is degreewise injective. Apply [lem-coef-sset-anodyne-pushout-product] with $i=b_n$ and with its anodyne map equal to $j$. It gives that
$$q_n:(\Delta^n\times K)\amalg_{\partial\Delta^n\times K}(\partial\Delta^n\times L)\longrightarrow\Delta^n\times L$$
is anodyne. Its left lifting property therefore applies to $E\to\Delta^0$ from step 3.

source.place: SSet.anodyneExtensions_pushoutObjObjι, lines 95-103; Kan model lifting classes as stated in the cited Kan-Quillen node.

proof.text: Consider an arbitrary square against $b_n$ for $r:\operatorname{Fun}(L,E)\to\operatorname{Fun}(K,E)$. A map $T\to\operatorname{Fun}(L,E)$ is, by the formula for this simplicial exponential in [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones], the same map $L\times T\to E$ under simplicial currying. Concretely evaluation sends $(\ell,t)$ in degree $m$ to the value at $(\ell,\mathrm{id}_{[m]})$ of the $m$-simplex corresponding to $t$; the inverse restricts a map $L\times T\to E$ along every simplex of $T$. Hence the two maps in the square are compatible maps $L\times\partial\Delta^n\to E$ and $K\times\Delta^n\to E$. Compatibility is equality on $K\times\partial\Delta^n$, so they give a map from the domain of $q_n$ to $E$, after switching the product coordinates. Step 4 supplies its extension to $\Delta^n\times L$. Switching coordinates back and currying gives a filler for the original square, with exactly its prescribed boundary and restriction. This works for every $n$, so $r$ has all the claimed boundary lifts.

source.place: Corollary 3.1.4.4, fully marked parameter argument; direct exponential adjunction and lifting-square calculation.

proof.text: The boundary characterization in [lem-coef-kan-quillen-right-proper] now says that $r$ is a trivial Kan fibration. The identity of steps 1-2 identifies this very restriction map with the marked restriction in the statement. When $n=0$, the boundary is empty and $q_0$ is $j$ itself, up to coordinate switches; the same lift therefore proves surjectivity on vertices. If $K$ is empty, weak equivalence forces $L$ to be empty as well, since a nonempty simplicial set has a vertex and its realization has a component; both mapping complexes are then terminal. If $C$ is empty and $K,L$ are nonempty, both mapping complexes are empty and restriction is the identity on the empty simplicial set, which has all boundary lifts vacuously. These checks also cover $K=L=\varnothing$ and impose no extra hypotheses.

source.place: Corollary 3.1.4.4; boundary lifting conclusion and direct empty-case checks.

proof.text: All maps and factorizations through the core above use subsets, degreewise products and pushouts of the input sets, and sets of maps between these sets. The standard simplices and their boundaries are finite. The core-Kan assertion and the anodyne lifting statements used above are relative to the fixed universe, so their fillers are maps between the same small simplicial sets. Thus the identity and restriction conclusion remain in the universe of the input, as stipulated in [def-weil-size-convention].

lean.statement: theorem marked_sharp_anodyne_restriction : (∃ (e : ∀ (K C : SSet.{u}) (_ : Quasicategory C), mapSharp (sharp K) (natural C) ≅ (ihom K).obj (Enhanced.core C).toSSet), (∀ (K C : SSet.{u}) (hC : Quasicategory C) (n m : SimplexCategoryᵒᵖ) (f : (mapSharp (sharp K) (natural C)).obj n) (x : K.obj m) (a : n ⟶ m), (((e K C hC).hom.app n f).app m a x).val = f.val.app m (x, SSet.stdSimplex.objEquiv.symm a.unop)) ∧ (∀ (K C : SSet.{u}) (hC : Quasicategory C), ∀ (K' : SSet.{u}) (r : K' ⟶ K), mapSharpPre (sharpMap r) (natural C) ≫ (e K' C hC).hom = (e K C hC).hom ≫ (MonoidalClosed.pre r).app (Enhanced.core C).toSSet) ∧ (∀ (K C D : SSet.{u}) (hC : Quasicategory C) (hD : Quasicategory D) (f : C ⟶ D), (e K C hC).hom ≫ (ihom K).map (Enhanced.coreMap f) = mapSharpPost (sharp K) (naturalMap f) ≫ (e K D hD).hom)) ∧ (∀ (K L C : SSet.{u}) (hC : Quasicategory C) (j : K ⟶ L), (∀ n : SimplexCategoryᵒᵖ, Function.Injective (j.app n)) → Enhanced.IsWeakHomotopyEquivalence j → SSet.modelCategoryQuillen.I.rlp (mapSharpPre (sharpMap j) (natural C)))
